org.portico.utils.messaging

Class ExtendedSuccessMessage

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.utils.messaging.ResponseMessage
      • org.portico.utils.messaging.ExtendedSuccessMessage
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Externalizable, Serializable

    public class ExtendedSuccessMessage
extends ResponseMessage
implements Externalizable
    This class represents a success response message and can contain any number of return values that should be passed back to the initiator of the request. This class also contains the notion of the "result" object, which is basically just a single, pre-named object that is used to identify the main or only object being returned. It is basically just a shortcut to avoid handlers from having to know ahead of time what the key used to identify the single result being returned is (a single return object is the most common case).

      • setResult

        public void setResult(Object resultObject)
        In each ExtendedSuccessMessage there is the notion of the "result" object. This is essentially an object bound to the key "result" in the return values. This method will set the given object as the result object (even if it is null), replacing the existing object if there is one.

      • getResult

        public <X> X getResult(Class<X> expectedClass)
        In each ExtendedSuccessMessage there is the notion of the "result" object. This is essentially an object bound to the key "result" in the return values. This method will fetch that object and return it (or null if there isn't an explicit result). This method lets you specify the expected type of the result object. If it exists, this method will cast it before returning. If the result object is of the wrong type, null will be returned.
